note: Bank card 'Water Act, 1974: the law that built the Pollution Control Boards'. Chapter teaches the Act (No. 6 of 1974), the Article 252 basis, CPCB constituted September 1974 (c16), Central Board under Section 3 and State Boards under Section 4 (c06, c07), CPCB's headline function (c09, c18) and the Section 25/26 consent system (c14, c40) — all three bank questions on this card are answerable from the chapter.

Bank card 'Air Act, 1981: consent before an industrial plant may run'. Chapter teaches the same CPCB/SPCB machinery serving the Air Act (c24), Section 21 consent from the State Board (c28), Section 22 excess-emission bar (c29) and the 1981 year — both bank questions answerable. Caveat: the card's statement that the Act was enacted under Article 253 is NOT taught — the fetched India Code text of the Air Act does not state an Article 253 basis (its preamble cites the 1972 Stockholm decisions, which the chapter does teach, c21). Source gap, disclosed in REPORT.md.

Bank card 'Environment (Protection) Act, 1986: the umbrella over all pollution law'. Chapter teaches the umbrella character (c61), Act 29 of 1986, in force 19 November 1986 (c31, c32), Section 3 powers (c35), Section 5 closure directions (c37), rule-making under Sections 6/25 as the parent of later rules (c38, c53) and the CPCB's technical-services role under the EPA (c17) — all three bank questions answerable. Caveat: the card's Bhopal-disaster trigger framing is NOT taught — no allowed-publisher (gov.in/nic.in) quote for it was fetched; the chapter teaches only the Stockholm basis stated in the Act's own preamble (c33). Source gap, disclosed in REPORT.md.

Bank card 'Consent to Establish, Consent to Operate — and the Red, Orange, Green, White ladder'. Chapter teaches CTE/CTO (c52), the consent sections (Water 25, Air 21 — c40), the 2016 PI bands Red 60+/Orange 41-59/Green 21-40/White up to 20 (c43), the White-category CTO exemption by intimation (c45) and the Red-category bar in ecologically fragile areas (c46) — all three bank questions answerable on the 2016 framework. The chapter additionally flags CPCB's January 2025 revised bands (Red >= 80) and the new Blue category (c50, c51) in an exam note, so a future paper using the revised bands is also covered.

WBCS 2019 Q148 asks the noise level above which noise is treated as pollution (official key: 80-99 dB, the physically painful threshold). The chapter teaches the statutory zone limits of the Noise Rules, 2000 (50-75 dB(A) by area, day/night) but NOT this ~80 dB physiological threshold — it appears in none of the fetched official sources. Partial coverage only; the specific keyed fact is a source gap.

WBCS 2023 Q163 asks which State/UT launched a '15-point Winter Action Plan' to control air pollution (Delhi). This is a current-affairs item about a state government's seasonal action plan, not part of the statutory framework (Acts, boards, consent, categories) this chapter teaches. Out of scope by design; not taught.

Clerkship 2009 (Session II) Q1 asks what a 'Green Bench' means — the special benches of High Courts / the Supreme Court that hear environmental cases. The chapter teaches the statutory tribunal route (NGT, 2010) but not the Green Bench concept of the higher judiciary; no fetched official source in this chapter covers it. Not taught; nearest taught neighbour is the NGT material in rules_enforcement.
